1	# Hybrid Simulator - Market Requirements Document
2	
3	Status: draft v0.1. Written 2026-05-28. Owner: Nick.
4	
5	Companion to `commercial_v1_roadmap.md` (engineering plan) and
6	`limitation.md` (current ROI envelope). This file is the *product*
7	view: who needs this, why the existing tool stack does not serve
8	them, and what we must deliver to claim the market.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Problem statement
13	
14	Pre-silicon performance evaluation today forces customers to pick
15	exactly one trade-off:
16	
17	- **QEMU**: runs at MHz, but tells you nothing about cycles.
18	- **Alioth (SystemC cycle-correlated)**: ~0.1-1 MIPS. Customer-facing,
19	  RTL-correlated. Booting Linux to a SPEC kernel takes hours-days.
20	- **Verilator (RTL cycle-exact)**: ~5-9 KHz on Andes RISC-V. Cannot
21	  reach a real workload's steady state in human time.
22	- **FPGA / emulator**: near-real speed, cycle-exact, but late in the
23	  schedule, expensive, and has almost no signal visibility.
24	
25	The single biggest gap: **"I want cycle-accurate measurement of a
26	small kernel, but the workload spends 99% of cycles in boring boot,
27	libc init, OS warmup, and dataset load."** No tool above answers
28	this without weeks of runtime or a tape-out.
29	
30	Hybrid simulator closes this gap by running the boring 99% in QEMU
31	and switching into a cycle-accurate simulator only for the
32	region of interest (ROI).
33	
34	---
35	
36	## 2. Target users
37	
38	| User | Today's pain | Hybrid_sim payoff |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| **Andes architect** evaluating a microarch change on a real workload | Re-runs full Verilator/Alioth for every tweak (days per iteration) | Boot once, re-measure ROI in minutes (100x-1000x faster iteration) |
41	| **Andes customer** sizing a SoC for their own workload | Cannot wait days; cannot get FPGA before tape-out | Ships hybrid_sim, runs their ELF, gets cycle figures in minutes |
42	| **SPEC / benchmark engineer** producing whole-program CPI | Fully cycle-accurate run is intractable | SimPoint clustering + per-phase cycle-exact measurement + weighted combine |
43	| **Pipeline / kanata trace consumer** | Trace file dominated by uninteresting boot | Record only the loop iterations that matter, byte-identical to a fully-RTL baseline |
44	| **DV engineer** chasing a perf anomaly that only appears after long warmup | Cannot reproduce in Verilator alone | Fast-forward in QEMU to the anomaly, then cycle-exact from there |
45	
46	---
47	
48	## 3. Market Requirements
49	
50	Numbered for traceability into the engineering roadmap.
51	
52	### MR-A - Linux-userspace ROI measurement
53	
54	A user shall be able to boot Linux (or any S/U-mode workload), reach
55	an application's hot loop, hand off to the cycle-accurate simulator,
56	measure the loop, and hand back.
57	
58	- **Status**: blocked. ROI is M-mode only today (`limitation.md` core
59	  rule). Requires Wave 2 of `commercial_v1_roadmap.md`: paging (L3),
60	  trap state (L4), priv restore (L6), PMP (L2), syscalls in ROI (L1).
61	- **Acceptance**: a fixture that boots Linux, runs a userspace
62	  benchmark kernel, returns a cycle count that agrees with a
63	  fully-RTL baseline within an explicit error budget.
64	
65	### MR-B - Whole-program estimate via SimPoint
66	
67	A user shall be able to point hybrid_sim at a long workload and
68	receive a weighted whole-program cycle estimate without running the
69	whole workload cycle-accurate.
70	
71	- **Status**: shipped at v0.x for M-mode workloads (`./hsim run
72	  --mode simpoint`); `commercial_v1_roadmap.md` Wave 5 (L14) adds
73	  CI bands and tuned warmup.
74	- **Acceptance**: estimate within 5-10% of fully-RTL for at least 3
75	  SPEC-class workloads.
76	
77	### MR-C - Customer-deliverable workload measurement
78	
79	An Andes customer with their own ELF shall be able to run that ELF
80	against hybrid_sim and get RTL-correlated cycle figures, without
81	needing FPGA hardware or RTL access.
82	
83	- **Status**: blocked on MR-A plus Andes vendor CSR parity
84	  (`commercial_v1_roadmap.md` Wave 3, L21) and trigger redesign
85	  (L12 - move off CSR `0x7C0`).
86	- **Acceptance**: a customer-style benchmark (closed-source ELF,
87	  Linux userspace, vendor-CSR usage) round-trips and produces a
88	  cycle count.
89	
90	### MR-D - Iterative microarch tweak loop
91	
92	An architect shall be able to change a microarch parameter, rebuild
93	the cycle-accurate simulator, and re-measure the same ROI without
94	re-running the boot phase.
95	
96	- **Status**: partially supported (QEMU phase is stable; vsim
97	  rebuild is independent). Wider envelope (MR-A) makes this usable
98	  on real workloads.
99	- **Acceptance**: edit-rebuild-measure cycle under 5 minutes for a
100	  kernel inside a Linux app.
101	
102	### MR-E - ROI-only pipeline trace recording
103	
104	A user shall be able to record kanata or Clarity-style pipeline
105	traces for exactly the iterations of interest, with byte-identical
106	output to a fully-RTL baseline over that window.
107	
108	- **Status**: shipped at v0.x for M-mode (kanata integration in
109	  Phase 4 of `hybrid_plan.md`).
110	- **Acceptance**: kanata diff is empty against a fully-RTL baseline
111	  for the recorded window after warmup.
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 4. Competitive positioning
116	
117	Single-tool view:
118	
119	| Tool | Speed (rough) | Cycle fidelity | Visibility | Available |
120	|---|---|---|---|---|
121	| QEMU (TCG) | 200-1000 MIPS | none | low | always |
122	| Alioth | 0.1-1 MIPS | RTL-correlated, small CPI gap | high (Clarity DB, HPM) | post pipeline model |
123	| Verilator | 1-50 KHz | cycle-exact (is the RTL) | very high (every wire) | when RTL exists |
124	| FPGA | 10-100 MHz | cycle-exact | very low (ILA only) | very late |
125	| **Hybrid_sim (QEMU + vsim)** | QEMU speed for boring code, vsim speed in ROI | cycle-exact in ROI | very high in ROI | needs RTL for vsim leg |
126	
127	The pitch is *not* "faster than FPGA". It is **"the only tool that
128	gives Verilator-grade fidelity on a kernel inside a workload that is
129	too long for Verilator to reach"**. That is a different axis.
130	
131	---
132	
133	## 5. Where hybrid_sim does NOT help
134	
135	Honest scope-out, to keep the MRD credible:
136	
137	- **Pre-RTL architecture exploration** (cache sizing, vector width,
138	  ROB depth before any RTL exists). Use Alioth alone.
139	- **RTL bug hunting outside the ROI**. If the bug is in boot or
140	  setup code, hybrid_sim runs that part on QEMU and never exercises
141	  the RTL there.
142	- **Full-system regression at near-real speed**. Use FPGA.
143	- **Functional bring-up of a new core**. Use QEMU alone.
144	- **Workloads with no clear ROI** (e.g. a long random benchmark
145	  with no hot kernel). SimPoint mode mitigates but cannot eliminate
146	  the problem.
147	
148	---
149	
150	## 6. v1 envelope vs market reach
151	
152	Today's narrow envelope (from `limitation.md`):
153	
154	- M-mode only, no S/U-mode (L6)
155	- No virtual memory (L3)
156	- Trap-free ROI (L4)
157	- No syscalls / semihosting in ROI (L1, blocker)
158	- No PMP enforcement (L2)
159	- Single hart (L8)
160	- No Andes vendor CSRs (L21)
161	- Hard-wired to `andes_ae350` + `ax45mpv` (L10)
162	
163	Implication: **MR-A, MR-C, MR-D cannot ship today.** Only MR-B (in
164	M-mode workloads) and MR-E (in M-mode workloads) are claimable.
165	
166	Ship targets (from `commercial_v1_roadmap.md`):
167	
168	| Milestone | Cumulative weeks | MRs claimable |
169	|---|---|---|
170	| Wave 0 + Wave 1 | 6 | MR-B (M-mode), MR-E (M-mode) - same as today, but loud about wrongness |
171	| MV beta (Wave 0+1 + L3+L4+L6) | ~18 | MR-A partial (S-mode, traps, paging), MR-B widened |
172	| Commercial v1.0 (Waves 0-5) | ~30 | MR-A, MR-B, MR-C, MR-D, MR-E |
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 7. Success metrics
177	
178	How we know hybrid_sim is winning its market:
179	
180	1. **Wall-clock speedup**: on a representative workload with ROI <
181	   1% of dynamic instructions, hybrid_sim produces a cycle figure at
182	   least **100x faster** than vsim-alone. Target stretch: 1000x.
183	2. **Accuracy**: per-ROI cycle figure within **<= 1%** of a fully-RTL
184	   baseline (excluding the documented microarch warm-up discontinuity).
185	3. **Whole-program estimate**: SimPoint output within **5-10%** of
186	   fully-RTL on at least 3 SPEC-class workloads.
187	4. **Customer adoption**: at least one external customer running
188	   their own ELF end-to-end under hybrid_sim.
189	5. **Time-to-first-result**: a new user goes from `git clone` to a
190	   working round-trip cycle figure in **under 30 minutes**.
191	
192	---
193	
194	## 8. Future direction - QEMU + Alioth
195	
196	The hybrid_sim architecture is *consumer-agnostic* at the boundary:
197	QEMU plugin drains state into `hybrid_state_v1`, the consumer
198	restores it. Today the consumer is vsim (Verilator). A natural
199	extension is **QEMU + Alioth**.
200	
201	Comparative pitch:
202	
203	| Stack | Boot Linux + measure kernel | Visibility | Customer-shippable |
204	|---|---|---|---|
205	| Alioth alone | hours-days | high | yes |
206	| QEMU + vsim (today) | minutes | very high | no (vsim needs RTL) |
207	| **QEMU + Alioth (future)** | **minutes** | **high (Clarity DB, HPM, customer config)** | **yes** |
208	
209	Strategic case: this would give Andes a customer-shippable
210	fast-forward story matching gem5's KVM->O3 switching, while
211	keeping Alioth's RTL-correlation and customer-config advantages.
212	The Alioth-vs-gem5 doc explicitly calls out
213	*"Mid-sim CPU swap: Not supported"* as an Alioth gap.
214	
215	Engineering scope (rough): port the consumer side from DMI Abstract
216	Commands to `afw::Module` state writes. Everything else - QEMU
217	plugin, wire format, mmap RAM, SimPoint clustering, orchestrator -
218	stays the same.
219	
220	This is NOT scoped into commercial v1.0. It is documented here to
221	keep the MRD honest about where the platform can go after v1.0.
222	
223	---
224	
225	## 9. Competitive landscape
226	
227	The "fast-forward boring code + cycle-accurate ROI" pattern has
228	commercial proof: Synopsys, Cadence, and Siemens all sell
229	million-dollar tools that do exactly this. The pattern has a market.
230	
231	Hybrid_sim's wedge is **not** "do this pattern better than ZeBu" -
232	it is **"do this pattern at zero cost, with Andes IP support out of
233	the box, for the customer tier that cannot afford Tier-1 emulator
234	capex"**.
235	
236	### 9.1 The competitor matrix
237	
238	| Tier | Tool | Fast side | Cycle side | Price |
239	|---|---|---|---|---|
240	| 1 | Synopsys ZeBu + Virtualizer | Virtualizer (TLM, MHz) | ZeBu FPGA emulator (10-100 MHz) | $M+ capex |
241	| 1 | Cadence Palladium + Helium | Helium (virtual platform) | Palladium Z2 emulator | $M+ capex |
242	| 1 | Siemens Veloce + Vista | Vista (VP) | Veloce Strato emulator | $M+ capex |
243	| 2 | Synopsys Imperas (acq. 2024) | OVPsim functional | Timing models / DPI to RTL | $K-M license |
244	| 2 | ARM Fast Models + Cycle Models | Fast Models | Cycle Models | $K-M license |
245	| 2 | Wind River Simics + Hindsight | Functional full-system | Cycle analysis | $K-M license |
246	| 3 | gem5 KVM -> O3CPU | KVM / AtomicSimpleCPU | O3CPU | Open source |
247	| 3 | Spike + RTL DPI bridges | Spike functional ISS | RTL via DPI | Open source / hobby |
248	| - | **hybrid_sim** | **QEMU 9.x** | **vsim (Verilator); Alioth in future** | **$0 internal** |
249	
250	Tier 1 is the canonical pattern: boot Linux in TLM, switch to a
251	multi-million-dollar FPGA emulator at the ROI. Used by Apple,
252	Qualcomm, Intel, AMD-tier vendors. Same pattern, premium hardware
253	on the cycle side.
254	
255	Tier 2 is the RISC-V / specialty mid-market. Imperas was the
256	dominant commercial RISC-V hybrid story before Synopsys bought it
257	in 2024.
258	
259	Tier 3 is the academic / open baseline. gem5's KVM -> O3CPU swap
260	is the *reference* pattern hybrid_sim follows.
261	
262	### 9.2 Where hybrid_sim wins
263	
264	- **Cost**: $0 vs $M+ for ZeBu/Palladium. Andes engineers and
265	  (future) customers pay zero per-seat.
266	- **Andes-specific output**: first-class kanata, Clarity DB, HPM
267	  counters, Andes vendor CSRs, ACE. Generic tools do not know about
268	  these.
269	- **No FPGA bring-up**: runs on any Linux laptop. ZeBu/Palladium
270	  need a board and weeks of partitioning per design point.
271	- **Customer-shippable** (with QEMU + Alioth path, Section 8):
272	  customers measure their workloads without ever touching RTL or
273	  FPGA bitstreams.
274	
275	### 9.3 Where hybrid_sim loses
276	
277	- **Cycle-side speed**: ZeBu/Palladium emulators run at 10-100 MHz;
278	  hybrid_sim's vsim leg runs at 5-9 KHz, ~10,000x slower. For ROIs
279	  that are themselves billions of cycles, commercial emulators
280	  still win.
281	- **OS-bearing workloads today**: ZeBu hybrid boots Linux; hybrid_sim
282	  is M-mode-only until Wave 2 of the roadmap closes L1-L6.
283	- **Maturity**: ZeBu/Palladium are 10+ years productized with full
284	  support contracts; hybrid_sim is alpha.
285	- **Generic ISA / SoC coverage**: ZeBu/Palladium are ISA-agnostic
286	  and customer-configurable; hybrid_sim is hard-wired to
287	  `andes_ae350` + `ax45mpv` until L10 closes.
288	
289	### 9.4 Target customer profile
290	
291	The commercial alternatives delineate the addressable market.
292	Hybrid_sim's most likely customer:
293	
294	- Mid-tier RISC-V SoC integrator with an Andes IP license.
295	- Cannot justify $M+ ZeBu/Palladium capex.
296	- Has perf-measurement needs beyond what QEMU alone provides.
297	- Today: bare-metal kernels. Wave 2 onward: Linux userspace.
298	- Wants Andes-correlated CPI figures, not generic numbers.
299	
300	The customer who **can** afford ZeBu **and** needs full-system Linux
301	at emulator speed is **not** our target. We compete in the tier
302	below.
303	
304	### 9.5 Risks from the commercial landscape
305	
306	- **Tier-1 price compression**: Synopsys / Cadence may discount
307	  hybrid solutions for RISC-V mid-tier customers; our cost wedge
308	  narrows.
309	- **Imperas under Synopsys**: now part of a Tier-1 vendor; may
310	  expand into Andes IP support. Monitor.
311	- **Customer-built in-house tools**: SiFive, MIPS, others may build
312	  similar internally. IP defensibility is weak; speed of delivery
313	  matters.
314	- **gem5 productization** (low probability): if a vendor
315	  productizes gem5 hybrid with RISC-V support, our open-source /
316	  cost story weakens.
317	
318	### 9.6 Reference case - ARM Fast Models + Cycle Models
319	
320	The closest commercial proof of a *customer-shippable* hybrid
321	pattern. Worth a detailed look because it informs both QEMU +
322	Alioth (Section 8) and the long-term encryption question.
323	
324	**Two products, one swap:**
325	
326	| Product | Role | Built from | Speed | Shippable? |
327	|---|---|---|---|---|
328	| Fast Models | Functional sim, SW dev, OS bring-up | Hand-written behavioral C++ | 100-500 MIPS | Yes (encrypted) |
329	| Cycle Models | Cycle-exact perf evaluation | RTL compiled via Carbon Model Studio | 10-100 KHz | Yes (encrypted) |
330	
331	ARM acquired Carbon Design Systems ~2015 for the cycle-side

# Hybrid Simulator - Market Requirements Document

Status: draft v0.1. Written 2026-05-28. Owner: Nick.

Companion to `commercial_v1_roadmap.md` (engineering plan) and
`limitation.md` (current ROI envelope). This file is the *product*
view: who needs this, why the existing tool stack does not serve
them, and what we must deliver to claim the market.

---

## 1. Problem statement

Pre-silicon performance evaluation today forces customers to pick
exactly one trade-off:

- **QEMU**: runs at MHz, but tells you nothing about cycles.
- **Alioth (SystemC cycle-correlated)**: ~0.1-1 MIPS. Customer-facing,
  RTL-correlated. Booting Linux to a SPEC kernel takes hours-days.
- **Verilator (RTL cycle-exact)**: ~5-9 KHz on Andes RISC-V. Cannot
  reach a real workload's steady state in human time.
- **FPGA / emulator**: near-real speed, cycle-exact, but late in the
  schedule, expensive, and has almost no signal visibility.

The single biggest gap: **"I want cycle-accurate measurement of a
small kernel, but the workload spends 99% of cycles in boring boot,
libc init, OS warmup, and dataset load."** No tool above answers
this without weeks of runtime or a tape-out.

Hybrid simulator closes this gap by running the boring 99% in QEMU
and switching into a cycle-accurate simulator only for the
region of interest (ROI).

---

## 2. Target users

| User | Today's pain | Hybrid_sim payoff |
|---|---|---|
| **Andes architect** evaluating a microarch change on a real workload | Re-runs full Verilator/Alioth for every tweak (days per iteration) | Boot once, re-measure ROI in minutes (100x-1000x faster iteration) |
| **Andes customer** sizing a SoC for their own workload | Cannot wait days; cannot get FPGA before tape-out | Ships hybrid_sim, runs their ELF, gets cycle figures in minutes |
| **SPEC / benchmark engineer** producing whole-program CPI | Fully cycle-accurate run is intractable | SimPoint clustering + per-phase cycle-exact measurement + weighted combine |
| **Pipeline / kanata trace consumer** | Trace file dominated by uninteresting boot | Record only the loop iterations that matter, byte-identical to a fully-RTL baseline |
| **DV engineer** chasing a perf anomaly that only appears after long warmup | Cannot reproduce in Verilator alone | Fast-forward in QEMU to the anomaly, then cycle-exact from there |

---

## 3. Market Requirements

Numbered for traceability into the engineering roadmap.

### MR-A - Linux-userspace ROI measurement

A user shall be able to boot Linux (or any S/U-mode workload), reach
an application's hot loop, hand off to the cycle-accurate simulator,
measure the loop, and hand back.

- **Status**: blocked. ROI is M-mode only today (`limitation.md` core
  rule). Requires Wave 2 of `commercial_v1_roadmap.md`: paging (L3),
  trap state (L4), priv restore (L6), PMP (L2), syscalls in ROI (L1).
- **Acceptance**: a fixture that boots Linux, runs a userspace
  benchmark kernel, returns a cycle count that agrees with a
  fully-RTL baseline within an explicit error budget.

### MR-B - Whole-program estimate via SimPoint

A user shall be able to point hybrid_sim at a long workload and
receive a weighted whole-program cycle estimate without running the
whole workload cycle-accurate.

- **Status**: shipped at v0.x for M-mode workloads (`./hsim run
  --mode simpoint`); `commercial_v1_roadmap.md` Wave 5 (L14) adds
  CI bands and tuned warmup.
- **Acceptance**: estimate within 5-10% of fully-RTL for at least 3
  SPEC-class workloads.

### MR-C - Customer-deliverable workload measurement

An Andes customer with their own ELF shall be able to run that ELF
against hybrid_sim and get RTL-correlated cycle figures, without
needing FPGA hardware or RTL access.

- **Status**: blocked on MR-A plus Andes vendor CSR parity
  (`commercial_v1_roadmap.md` Wave 3, L21) and trigger redesign
  (L12 - move off CSR `0x7C0`).
- **Acceptance**: a customer-style benchmark (closed-source ELF,
  Linux userspace, vendor-CSR usage) round-trips and produces a
  cycle count.

### MR-D - Iterative microarch tweak loop

An architect shall be able to change a microarch parameter, rebuild
the cycle-accurate simulator, and re-measure the same ROI without
re-running the boot phase.

- **Status**: partially supported (QEMU phase is stable; vsim
  rebuild is independent). Wider envelope (MR-A) makes this usable
  on real workloads.
- **Acceptance**: edit-rebuild-measure cycle under 5 minutes for a
  kernel inside a Linux app.

### MR-E - ROI-only pipeline trace recording

A user shall be able to record kanata or Clarity-style pipeline
traces for exactly the iterations of interest, with byte-identical
output to a fully-RTL baseline over that window.

- **Status**: shipped at v0.x for M-mode (kanata integration in
  Phase 4 of `hybrid_plan.md`).
- **Acceptance**: kanata diff is empty against a fully-RTL baseline
  for the recorded window after warmup.

---

## 4. Competitive positioning

Single-tool view:

| Tool | Speed (rough) | Cycle fidelity | Visibility | Available |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QEMU (TCG) | 200-1000 MIPS | none | low | always |
| Alioth | 0.1-1 MIPS | RTL-correlated, small CPI gap | high (Clarity DB, HPM) | post pipeline model |
| Verilator | 1-50 KHz | cycle-exact (is the RTL) | very high (every wire) | when RTL exists |
| FPGA | 10-100 MHz | cycle-exact | very low (ILA only) | very late |
| **Hybrid_sim (QEMU + vsim)** | QEMU speed for boring code, vsim speed in ROI | cycle-exact in ROI | very high in ROI | needs RTL for vsim leg |

The pitch is *not* "faster than FPGA". It is **"the only tool that
gives Verilator-grade fidelity on a kernel inside a workload that is
too long for Verilator to reach"**. That is a different axis.

---

## 5. Where hybrid_sim does NOT help

Honest scope-out, to keep the MRD credible:

- **Pre-RTL architecture exploration** (cache sizing, vector width,
  ROB depth before any RTL exists). Use Alioth alone.
- **RTL bug hunting outside the ROI**. If the bug is in boot or
  setup code, hybrid_sim runs that part on QEMU and never exercises
  the RTL there.
- **Full-system regression at near-real speed**. Use FPGA.
- **Functional bring-up of a new core**. Use QEMU alone.
- **Workloads with no clear ROI** (e.g. a long random benchmark
  with no hot kernel). SimPoint mode mitigates but cannot eliminate
  the problem.

---

## 6. v1 envelope vs market reach

Today's narrow envelope (from `limitation.md`):

- M-mode only, no S/U-mode (L6)
- No virtual memory (L3)
- Trap-free ROI (L4)
- No syscalls / semihosting in ROI (L1, blocker)
- No PMP enforcement (L2)
- Single hart (L8)
- No Andes vendor CSRs (L21)
- Hard-wired to `andes_ae350` + `ax45mpv` (L10)

Implication: **MR-A, MR-C, MR-D cannot ship today.** Only MR-B (in
M-mode workloads) and MR-E (in M-mode workloads) are claimable.

Ship targets (from `commercial_v1_roadmap.md`):

| Milestone | Cumulative weeks | MRs claimable |
|---|---|---|
| Wave 0 + Wave 1 | 6 | MR-B (M-mode), MR-E (M-mode) - same as today, but loud about wrongness |
| MV beta (Wave 0+1 + L3+L4+L6) | ~18 | MR-A partial (S-mode, traps, paging), MR-B widened |
| Commercial v1.0 (Waves 0-5) | ~30 | MR-A, MR-B, MR-C, MR-D, MR-E |

---

## 7. Success metrics

How we know hybrid_sim is winning its market:

1. **Wall-clock speedup**: on a representative workload with ROI <
   1% of dynamic instructions, hybrid_sim produces a cycle figure at
   least **100x faster** than vsim-alone. Target stretch: 1000x.
2. **Accuracy**: per-ROI cycle figure within **<= 1%** of a fully-RTL
   baseline (excluding the documented microarch warm-up discontinuity).
3. **Whole-program estimate**: SimPoint output within **5-10%** of
   fully-RTL on at least 3 SPEC-class workloads.
4. **Customer adoption**: at least one external customer running
   their own ELF end-to-end under hybrid_sim.
5. **Time-to-first-result**: a new user goes from `git clone` to a
   working round-trip cycle figure in **under 30 minutes**.

---

## 8. Future direction - QEMU + Alioth

The hybrid_sim architecture is *consumer-agnostic* at the boundary:
QEMU plugin drains state into `hybrid_state_v1`, the consumer
restores it. Today the consumer is vsim (Verilator). A natural
extension is **QEMU + Alioth**.

Comparative pitch:

| Stack | Boot Linux + measure kernel | Visibility | Customer-shippable |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alioth alone | hours-days | high | yes |
| QEMU + vsim (today) | minutes | very high | no (vsim needs RTL) |
| **QEMU + Alioth (future)** | **minutes** | **high (Clarity DB, HPM, customer config)** | **yes** |

Strategic case: this would give Andes a customer-shippable
fast-forward story matching gem5's KVM->O3 switching, while
keeping Alioth's RTL-correlation and customer-config advantages.
The Alioth-vs-gem5 doc explicitly calls out
*"Mid-sim CPU swap: Not supported"* as an Alioth gap.

Engineering scope (rough): port the consumer side from DMI Abstract
Commands to `afw::Module` state writes. Everything else - QEMU
plugin, wire format, mmap RAM, SimPoint clustering, orchestrator -
stays the same.

This is NOT scoped into commercial v1.0. It is documented here to
keep the MRD honest about where the platform can go after v1.0.

---

## 9. Competitive landscape

The "fast-forward boring code + cycle-accurate ROI" pattern has
commercial proof: Synopsys, Cadence, and Siemens all sell
million-dollar tools that do exactly this. The pattern has a market.

Hybrid_sim's wedge is **not** "do this pattern better than ZeBu" -
it is **"do this pattern at zero cost, with Andes IP support out of
the box, for the customer tier that cannot afford Tier-1 emulator
capex"**.

### 9.1 The competitor matrix

| Tier | Tool | Fast side | Cycle side | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Synopsys ZeBu + Virtualizer | Virtualizer (TLM, MHz) | ZeBu FPGA emulator (10-100 MHz) | $M+ capex |
| 1 | Cadence Palladium + Helium | Helium (virtual platform) | Palladium Z2 emulator | $M+ capex |
| 1 | Siemens Veloce + Vista | Vista (VP) | Veloce Strato emulator | $M+ capex |
| 2 | Synopsys Imperas (acq. 2024) | OVPsim functional | Timing models / DPI to RTL | $K-M license |
| 2 | ARM Fast Models + Cycle Models | Fast Models | Cycle Models | $K-M license |
| 2 | Wind River Simics + Hindsight | Functional full-system | Cycle analysis | $K-M license |
| 3 | gem5 KVM -> O3CPU | KVM / AtomicSimpleCPU | O3CPU | Open source |
| 3 | Spike + RTL DPI bridges | Spike functional ISS | RTL via DPI | Open source / hobby |
| - | **hybrid_sim** | **QEMU 9.x** | **vsim (Verilator); Alioth in future** | **$0 internal** |

Tier 1 is the canonical pattern: boot Linux in TLM, switch to a
multi-million-dollar FPGA emulator at the ROI. Used by Apple,
Qualcomm, Intel, AMD-tier vendors. Same pattern, premium hardware
on the cycle side.

Tier 2 is the RISC-V / specialty mid-market. Imperas was the
dominant commercial RISC-V hybrid story before Synopsys bought it
in 2024.

Tier 3 is the academic / open baseline. gem5's KVM -> O3CPU swap
is the *reference* pattern hybrid_sim follows.

### 9.2 Where hybrid_sim wins

- **Cost**: $0 vs $M+ for ZeBu/Palladium. Andes engineers and
  (future) customers pay zero per-seat.
- **Andes-specific output**: first-class kanata, Clarity DB, HPM
  counters, Andes vendor CSRs, ACE. Generic tools do not know about
  these.
- **No FPGA bring-up**: runs on any Linux laptop. ZeBu/Palladium
  need a board and weeks of partitioning per design point.
- **Customer-shippable** (with QEMU + Alioth path, Section 8):
  customers measure their workloads without ever touching RTL or
  FPGA bitstreams.

### 9.3 Where hybrid_sim loses

- **Cycle-side speed**: ZeBu/Palladium emulators run at 10-100 MHz;
  hybrid_sim's vsim leg runs at 5-9 KHz, ~10,000x slower. For ROIs
  that are themselves billions of cycles, commercial emulators
  still win.
- **OS-bearing workloads today**: ZeBu hybrid boots Linux; hybrid_sim
  is M-mode-only until Wave 2 of the roadmap closes L1-L6.
- **Maturity**: ZeBu/Palladium are 10+ years productized with full
  support contracts; hybrid_sim is alpha.
- **Generic ISA / SoC coverage**: ZeBu/Palladium are ISA-agnostic
  and customer-configurable; hybrid_sim is hard-wired to
  `andes_ae350` + `ax45mpv` until L10 closes.

### 9.4 Target customer profile

The commercial alternatives delineate the addressable market.
Hybrid_sim's most likely customer:

- Mid-tier RISC-V SoC integrator with an Andes IP license.
- Cannot justify $M+ ZeBu/Palladium capex.
- Has perf-measurement needs beyond what QEMU alone provides.
- Today: bare-metal kernels. Wave 2 onward: Linux userspace.
- Wants Andes-correlated CPI figures, not generic numbers.

The customer who **can** afford ZeBu **and** needs full-system Linux
at emulator speed is **not** our target. We compete in the tier
below.

### 9.5 Risks from the commercial landscape

- **Tier-1 price compression**: Synopsys / Cadence may discount
  hybrid solutions for RISC-V mid-tier customers; our cost wedge
  narrows.
- **Imperas under Synopsys**: now part of a Tier-1 vendor; may
  expand into Andes IP support. Monitor.
- **Customer-built in-house tools**: SiFive, MIPS, others may build
  similar internally. IP defensibility is weak; speed of delivery
  matters.
- **gem5 productization** (low probability): if a vendor
  productizes gem5 hybrid with RISC-V support, our open-source /
  cost story weakens.

### 9.6 Reference case - ARM Fast Models + Cycle Models

The closest commercial proof of a *customer-shippable* hybrid
pattern. Worth a detailed look because it informs both QEMU +
Alioth (Section 8) and the long-term encryption question.

**Two products, one swap:**

| Product | Role | Built from | Speed | Shippable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fast Models | Functional sim, SW dev, OS bring-up | Hand-written behavioral C++ | 100-500 MIPS | Yes (encrypted) |
| Cycle Models | Cycle-exact perf evaluation | RTL compiled via Carbon Model Studio | 10-100 KHz | Yes (encrypted) |

ARM acquired Carbon Design Systems ~2015 for the cycle-side
tooling. Carbon Model Studio compiles RTL into an **encrypted**
cycle-accurate C++ model. Customer gets the binary, runs it, gets
cycle figures, **cannot recover the RTL**. The same problem hsim's
vsim leg has - solved by an explicit encryption pipeline.

Both products share the **CADI** (Component Architecture Debug
Interface). Virtual Platform tools (ARM System Generator,
Synopsys Virtualizer, Cadence VSP) swap Fast Models for Cycle
Models at the ROI. Identical pattern to hsim.

**Two strategic lessons for Andes:**

1. **Alioth already covers most of the Fast Models role**, with
   the bonus of RTL-correlated cycle counts that ARM Fast Models
   lack. QEMU + Alioth (Section 8) gives us most of ARM's
   two-tier value in one tier.
2. **For true cycle-exact customer delivery**, the answer is
   encryption tooling around Verilator output (Carbon-style),
   not shipping vanilla vsim binaries. Future engineering bet,
   scoped beyond commercial v1.0.

**What ARM does not do that hsim does:**

- ARM Cycle Models are per-core; customer brings their own NoC
  and memory controller. Alioth ships the full cluster
  (MSS + ACE + CM500).
- No bundled SimPoint, kanata, or trigger / handoff layer - all
  sold separately by Synopsys / Cadence. Hsim bundles these.

Even compared to ARM's mature offering, hsim's
"all-in-one + Andes-specific" packaging is differentiation, not
parity.

---

## 10. Open product questions

For PM / lead review:

- **Customer license model**: does hybrid_sim ship inside the same
  customer-facing Alioth bundle, or as a separate add-on?
- **QEMU dependency**: customers run on whatever QEMU we tell them
  to. Do we fork (long-term maintenance) or pin to upstream
  (compatibility risk)?
- **Closed-source customer ELFs**: does the magic-CSR trigger
  approach require customer-source modification, or does PC-trigger
  mode (no source change) cover the common case?
- **Andes vendor CSR exposure**: which Andes-custom CSRs are
  customer-visible and must round-trip? L21 lists 9; do we need
  more?
- **Multi-hart priority**: which customers are blocked on multi-hart
  (L8 / Wave 4)? If none yet, defer beyond v1.0.

---

## 11. References

- `commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - engineering plan, 6 waves, 21
  numbered limitations closed.
- `docs/limitation.md` - current ROI envelope, ground truth.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` - user-facing workflows and modes.
- `hybrid_plan.md` - original design rationale and phased delivery.
- `specs/hybrid-sim-gem5-switch-parity.md` - parity analysis with
  gem5's switchable-CPU mechanism.
- Alioth: `~/work/Alioth/doc/alioth-vs-gem5.md` for the
  "Mid-sim CPU swap: Not supported" gap that QEMU+Alioth would
  close.

questions.question: Which existing MRD content do you want to keep vs rewrite for the commercial pivot?

options.label: Rewrite from scratch
options.description: Drop the internal-tool framing. New MRD targets external buyers, with pricing, licensing, support, IP protection, packaging as first-class sections.

options.label: Augment existing (Recommended)
options.description: Keep Sections 1-9 (problem, users, MRs, competitive). Add new sections: business model, license/delivery, IP protection, support, productization gaps. Cheaper to maintain.

options.label: Split into two docs
options.description: Keep current MRD as internal engineering plan. Create new commercial-MRD.md for the product-go-to-market view. FRS as third doc.

questions.question: Which cycle-side engine is the v1.0 commercial product?

options.label: QEMU + Alioth only (Recommended)
options.description: Customer-shippable from day one (Alioth is already customer-facing). Drops vsim/Verilator entirely from the commercial product. Internal users still get vsim path.

options.label: QEMU + vsim only
options.description: Ships vsim binary as the cycle engine. Requires Carbon-style RTL encryption pipeline before customer ship. Adds 6-12 months.

options.label: Both, customer chooses
options.description: Two SKUs: hsim-Alioth (customer) and hsim-vsim (internal+DV). Same orchestrator/QEMU/wire-format. Doubles QA matrix.

questions.question: Which competitor tier do we price against?

options.label: Tier 2 mid-market (Recommended)
options.description: $K-M/year like ARM Cycle Models, Imperas, Wind River Simics. Andes-IP-bundled, customer-shippable. Realistic for Andes' customer base.

options.label: Tier 3 open / freemium
options.description: Open-source core (like gem5), paid Andes-IP add-on or support. Wider adoption but lower revenue per seat.

options.label: Tier 1 premium
options.description: Compete head-on with ZeBu/Palladium/Veloce at $M+ capex. Unrealistic without FPGA-class cycle-side speed; not recommended.

questions.question: Is IP encryption (Carbon-style) in v1.0 scope or future?

options.label: v1.0 must include encryption (Recommended)
options.description: Cycle-side binary is encrypted/obfuscated so customers cannot recover Andes RTL or microarch internals. Hard requirement for any RTL-sourced engine.

options.label: v1.0 ships unencrypted, customer-shippable by Alioth-only path
options.description: Skip encryption by shipping Alioth (already customer-facing, not RTL-derived). Encryption deferred to vsim-path post-v1.0.

options.label: Encryption post-v1.0
options.description: Document as risk; ship v1.0 to design-partner customers under NDA only. Defer encryption tooling.

questions.question: What level of FRS detail do you want now?

options.label: Outline + key requirements (Recommended)
options.description: Section structure with FR-1xx through FR-9xx requirement IDs, each with one-line acceptance criteria. ~10-15 pages. Detail later per section.

options.label: Full detailed FRS
options.description: Every requirement fully specified with inputs, outputs, edge cases, acceptance tests. ~40-60 pages. Slow to draft, slow to review.

options.label: One-page summary first
options.description: Top-20 functional requirements only, single page. Build out after PM review.

# Hybrid Simulator - Market Requirements Document

Status: draft v1.0 (commercial rewrite). Written 2026-05-29.
Owner: Nick. Audience: PM, BU lead, Sales engineering, Legal.

Companion docs:
- `FRS.md` - functional requirements specification (engineering contract)
- `commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - engineering plan
- `docs/limitation.md` - current ROI envelope (alpha)

This document is the **product** view, written for a paying
external buyer. The previous draft (v0.1) framed hybrid_sim as an
Andes-internal acceleration tool. This rewrite repositions it as a
commercial Tier-2 EDA product competing with ARM Cycle Models,
Synopsys Imperas, and Wind River Simics-class hybrid offerings.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

**Product name (working)**: Andes HybridSim
**Category**: Cycle-accurate hybrid simulator for RISC-V SoCs
**Cycle engine**: vsim (Verilator-derived, encrypted RTL pipeline)
**Fast engine**: QEMU 9.x with Andes plugin
**Target customer**: Andes IP licensees doing pre-silicon perf work
**Tier / price band**: Tier 2, $K-M/year per-seat or per-project
**Ship target**: Commercial v1.0 in ~12 months (engineering) +
6-12 months (encryption tooling) = ~18-24 months from today
**Differentiation**: only Tier-2 hybrid product with first-class
Andes IP (vendor CSRs, ACE, AndeStar V5 extensions) and zero FPGA
capex requirement

**The one-line pitch**: "Cycle-exact RISC-V perf measurement on
real customer workloads, without an FPGA emulator or a multi-year
RTL learning curve."

---

## 2. Product Definition

What the customer buys:

| Component | Delivery | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `hsim` driver CLI | binary | orchestrates QEMU->vsim->QEMU handoff |
| QEMU (Andes fork) | binary + plugin SO | fast-forward engine, runs boring 99% |
| vsim cycle engine | **encrypted** binary | cycle-exact ROI measurement, RTL-derived but not RTL-recoverable |
| State transport library | linked into both | `hybrid_state_v1` wire format, mmap RAM |
| Trigger toolkit | linked + headers | magic-CSR, PC-watch, icount, SimPoint |
| Pipeline trace converter | binary | kanata / Clarity DB output |
| Reference flow | scripts + sample workloads | bare-metal kernel, Linux userspace, SPEC-class harness |
| License daemon | binary | per-seat / per-project enforcement |
| Documentation | PDF + HTML | user guide, ABI reference, integration guide |
| Support | contracted | tiered SLA |

What the customer does NOT get:
- Raw Verilator C++ output (encrypted only)
- Andes RTL or microarch internals
- Source of the cycle engine
- QEMU source (binary only; upstream QEMU available separately)

---

## 3. Target Market & Buyer Personas

### 3.1 Primary buyer: Andes IP licensee SoC integrator

| Attribute | Profile |
|---|---|
| Company size | 50-2000 engineers; cannot justify $M+ ZeBu capex |
| Andes IP | one or more of AX25 / AX27 / AX45 / AX46 / D23v |
| Workload class | OS + userspace apps, AI inference kernels, networking dataplane |
| Pain | QEMU is too coarse; FPGA is too late; Alioth alone is too slow on real workloads |
| Buying authority | Engineering VP + IT procurement; budget cycle 6-12 months |
| Price tolerance | $20K-200K/seat/year, $200K-2M project license |

### 3.2 Secondary buyer: research lab / university with industry tie-in

| Attribute | Profile |
|---|---|
| Use case | Microarchitecture research, comparative perf studies |
| Procurement | Grant-funded; multi-year |
| Price tolerance | Academic discount tier; $5K-20K/seat/year |
| Value to Andes | Reference publications, conference visibility, talent pipeline |

### 3.3 Personas at the buying customer

| Role | What they care about |
|---|---|
| **SoC Architect** | accuracy vs RTL, modeling fidelity of vendor CSRs |
| **Perf Engineer** | wall-clock turnaround, SimPoint coverage, kanata output |
| **DV Engineer** | reproducibility, deterministic mode, log capture |
| **Engineering VP / buyer** | total cost vs FPGA capex, support SLA, lifecycle |
| **Legal / IP officer** | encryption guarantees, no RTL leakage, license terms |
| **IT / DevOps** | install footprint, license server, CI integration |

---

## 4. Market Sizing & Opportunity

Rough TAM estimate (top-down):

- Andes IP active licensees: ~300 worldwide (public Andes 2025 figures)
- Fraction doing serious pre-silicon perf work: ~30% = ~90 accounts
- Fraction with ROI-style workloads (OS + hot kernel): ~60% = ~54 accounts
- Realistic 3-year capture rate: 20% = ~11 paying accounts
- Average deal size: $100K-500K/year
- Year-3 ARR target: $1.1M-5.5M

Adjacent expansion:
- Non-Andes RISC-V vendors (SiFive, MIPS, Tenstorrent) could license
  the QEMU plugin + state transport without Andes-specific vendor
  CSRs. Out of scope for v1.0 but TAM-meaningful.
- Internal Andes engineering teams (~200 engineers) consume the
  product at internal cost; counts as cost avoidance vs ZeBu rental.

---

## 5. Competitive Positioning

### 5.1 Competitive matrix (commercial Tier 2 focus)

| Product | Vendor | Strength | Weakness vs HybridSim | Price band |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARM Cycle Models + Fast Models | ARM | mature, encrypted, CADI ecosystem | ARM-only ISA; no Andes IP; per-core not full cluster | $100K-1M/yr |
| Imperas (now Synopsys) | Synopsys | RISC-V leader; DPI-to-RTL | functional ISS + RTL bridge, not true hybrid; expensive | $200K-2M/yr |
| Wind River Simics + Hindsight | Wind River | full-system; large install base | not cycle-exact; weak RISC-V perf modeling | $50K-500K/yr |
| **Andes HybridSim** | **Andes** | **first-class Andes IP, $0 cycle-side capex, bundled SimPoint/kanata** | **alpha today; Andes ISA only** | **$K-M/yr** |

Tier 1 (ZeBu/Palladium/Veloce) is explicitly not our competitive
target. They serve customers who already have $M+ FPGA capex.

Tier 3 (gem5, Spike+DPI) is not our competitive target either.
Open-source pulls revenue to zero; we ship Andes IP correlation as
a paid product.

### 5.2 The wedge

Three things competitors do not deliver together:

1. **First-class Andes IP modeling** - vendor CSRs, ACE, AndeStar V5,
   Andes platform (AE350-class) out of the box. ARM and Imperas
   require customer integration work; Wind River is functional-only.
2. **Zero FPGA capex** - runs on a Linux workstation. ZeBu/Palladium
   need a $M+ board.
3. **Bundled SimPoint + kanata + handoff orchestrator** - competitors
   sell these as separate add-ons or do not ship them at all.

### 5.3 Honest losses

- vsim cycle-side speed (5-50 KHz) is 1000-10000x slower than ZeBu
  emulator (10-100 MHz). For ROIs longer than ~1B cycles, ZeBu wins.
  Mitigation: SimPoint clustering shrinks effective ROI.
- ISA coverage is RISC-V Andes-only. ARM Cycle Models cover ARM
  ecosystem; Imperas covers broad RISC-V. Mitigation: deepen Andes
  IP support to make depth beat breadth.
- Maturity: ARM Cycle Models are 10+ years productized. Our v1.0
  is a fresh product. Mitigation: design-partner program before
  general availability.

---

## 6. Business Model

### 6.1 Pricing structure

Three SKUs:

| SKU | Audience | Includes | Price guidance |
|---|---|---|---|
| **HybridSim Workstation** | per-seat developer | full feature set, 1 named seat | $40K-80K/yr |
| **HybridSim Project** | per-project team | floating license pool (5-25 seats) | $200K-1M/yr |
| **HybridSim Academic** | universities, labs | feature-limited (no kanata export, no SimPoint estimate report) | $5K-15K/yr |

Add-ons (post-v1.0):
- Linux/SMP support pack (multi-hart, S/U-mode beyond v1.0 envelope)
- Custom Andes IP variant support (one-off NRE)
- Premium SLA (24h response, dedicated FAE)

### 6.2 License enforcement

- Network license daemon (FlexLM-class) per industry norm
- Node-locked option for air-gapped customers (HSM-bound)
- Floating pool with checkout / checkin
- Per-feature flags (kanata, SimPoint, vendor CSR pack)
- License expiry triggers graceful shutdown with checkpoint export

### 6.3 Delivery channels

- Direct (Andes sales) for top-50 accounts
- Distributor / reseller for long tail (e.g. through Andes regional
  partners in Japan, EU, US)
- Evaluation: 30-day full-feature trial under EULA, node-locked

---

## 7. Market Requirements

Numbered MRs for traceability into FRS.md. Each MR has a status
relative to v1.0 ship.

### MR-A - Cycle-exact ROI measurement on customer workloads

Customer provides their own ELF (closed source). HybridSim
fast-forwards in QEMU, switches to cycle engine at ROI, returns a
cycle figure correlated with RTL within an explicit error budget.

- Acceptance: closed-source customer ELF round-trips; cycle figure
  agrees with fully-RTL baseline within 1% on the ROI window.

### MR-B - Linux + userspace ROI

Boot Linux, reach userspace hot loop, hand off to cycle engine,
measure, hand back to QEMU.

- Acceptance: at least 3 SPEC-class workloads under Linux userspace
  ship a cycle figure end-to-end.

### MR-C - Whole-program estimate via SimPoint

Long workload, no explicit ROI. SimPoint clustering picks
representative regions, cycle engine measures each, weighted
combine produces a whole-program estimate.

- Acceptance: weighted estimate within 5-10% of fully-RTL on at
  least 3 SPEC-class workloads.

### MR-D - Closed-source RTL protection (encryption)

Cycle engine is RTL-derived (via Verilator) but the shipped binary
must not allow recovery of Andes RTL or microarch internals.

- Acceptance: third-party reverse-engineering audit confirms no
  RTL recoverable from shipped binary; license + IP officer sign-off.

### MR-E - Andes vendor CSR and ACE parity

All customer-visible Andes vendor CSRs and ACE coherence flows
round-trip across the handoff with bit-exact semantics.

- Acceptance: vendor-CSR conformance test suite passes 100%; ACE
  coherence regression passes on multi-hart workloads.

### MR-F - Pipeline trace export (kanata)

Customer can record kanata-format pipeline traces for the cycle
window with output byte-identical to a fully-RTL baseline.

- Acceptance: kanata diff against fully-RTL baseline is empty for
  the post-warmup window.

### MR-G - Iterative microarch tweak loop

Architect changes a cycle-engine parameter (cache size, ROB depth),
rebuilds engine only, re-runs measurement against the same QEMU
checkpoint without re-running boot.

- Acceptance: edit-rebuild-measure cycle under 5 minutes on a
  reference workload.

### MR-H - Multi-hart support

At least 4 harts in the cycle engine with coherent state transport
through ACE.

- Acceptance: a 4-hart parallel kernel round-trips and produces a
  cycle figure within 1% of fully-RTL baseline.

### MR-I - Determinism and reproducibility

Identical inputs (ELF + config + seed) produce bit-identical cycle
counts and pipeline traces across runs and hosts.

- Acceptance: a reproducibility test suite runs the same workload
  on 3 different hosts; all outputs bit-identical.

### MR-J - CI / batch integration

The product runs unattended in a CI environment. License daemon,
checkpointing, error reporting, and exit codes are CI-friendly.

- Acceptance: a reference CI pipeline (GitLab / Jenkins) runs 20
  workloads in parallel, collects results, no manual intervention.

### MR-K - First-class observability

Every handoff, trigger, and state transport event is logged with
structured key=value format. Errors are actionable, not "internal
error".

- Acceptance: a deliberate state-corruption injection produces a
  log message identifying the corrupted register and the handoff
  phase. No silent failures.

---

## 8. Go-to-Market & Delivery

### 8.1 Design-partner phase (months 0-6 post-engineering complete)

- 3-5 named Andes customers under NDA evaluate pre-GA build
- Free use under design-partner agreement; required to give
  feedback and bug reports
- Goal: prove MR-A + MR-B on real customer workloads before GA

### 8.2 Controlled GA (months 6-12)

- Direct sales to ~10 accounts at full price
- Quarterly feature releases
- Dedicated FAE per top-3 account

### 8.3 Broad GA (year 2+)

- Distributor channel opens
- Academic SKU launches
- Add-on packs (multi-hart, vendor IP variants) release

### 8.4 Onboarding goal

Customer goes from license activation to first valid cycle figure
on their own workload in **under 1 working day** with documentation
alone, no FAE intervention.

---

## 9. Success Metrics

### 9.1 Product KPIs

| Metric | v1.0 target | Year-2 target |
|---|---|---|
| Wall-clock speedup vs vsim-alone (1% ROI workload) | 100x | 1000x |
| Per-ROI accuracy vs fully-RTL | <= 1% | <= 0.5% |
| SimPoint whole-program accuracy | 5-10% | 3-5% |
| Time-to-first-result for new user | 1 day | 2 hours |
| Determinism rate across hosts | 100% bit-identical | 100% bit-identical |

### 9.2 Business KPIs

| Metric | Year-1 | Year-3 |
|---|---|---|
| Paying accounts | 3 | 11 |
| ARR | $300K | $2M-5M |
| Design-partner -> paying conversion | 60% | 75% |
| Customer renewal rate | n/a | >= 80% |
| Net Promoter Score | n/a | >= 30 |

---

## 10. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Encryption tooling adds 6-12 months | ship slip | high | start encryption track in parallel with engineering Wave 1; consider Carbon-style external partner |
| ZeBu price compression for RISC-V mid-market | margin erosion | medium | deepen Andes IP integration; sell on TCO not list price |
| Imperas under Synopsys expands into Andes IP | direct competitor | medium | move first; lock design partners |
| Customer demands ISA beyond Andes | scope creep | medium | charter Andes-only for v1.0; revisit at v2.0 |
| Verilator licensing review for commercial redistribution | legal block | low | LGPL compliance audit before alpha; consider clean-room or commercial Verilator |
| Customer workloads break v1.0 envelope (S/U-mode, paging) | scope gap | high | publish envelope explicitly (FRS); roadmap visible to customer |
| vsim cycle-side too slow for billion-cycle ROIs | win-rate drop | medium | SimPoint coverage; multi-instance parallel measurement |

---

## 11. Roadmap to v1.0

Engineering (from `commercial_v1_roadmap.md`):

| Wave | Closes | Cumulative weeks |
|---|---|---|
| Wave 0 | tooling, CI, regression harness | 3 |
| Wave 1 | M-mode loud-failure, basic deliverables | 6 |
| Wave 2 | S/U-mode, paging, traps, PMP (L1-L6) | 18 |
| Wave 3 | Andes vendor CSR, ACE, trigger redesign | 22 |
| Wave 4 | multi-hart (L8) | 26 |
| Wave 5 | SimPoint productization (L14), CI bands | 30 |

Productization (new, parallel track):

| Track | Closes | Weeks |
|---|---|---|
| Encryption pipeline | MR-D | 24-48 |
| License daemon | MR-J | 12 |
| Installer / packaging | section 2 deliverables | 8 |
| Documentation set | section 8 onboarding goal | 12 (continuous) |
| Support tooling (bug capture, telemetry, opt-in) | section 8 | 8 |
| Design-partner program | section 8.1 | continuous |

Critical path: **encryption pipeline** (24-48 weeks). Cannot ship
to customer without it (MR-D).

---

## 12. Open Product Questions

For BU lead and PM review:

- **Pricing**: confirm $40K-80K/seat is acceptable in the Andes
  customer base. Sales has data points.
- **License model**: per-seat vs per-project ratio target?
- **Encryption partner**: build in-house (24-48 weeks) or contract
  (Carbon-style external vendor, faster but adds royalty)?
- **Verilator commercial path**: are we LGPL-clean for
  redistribution, or do we need a commercial Verilator license?
- **First design partners**: which 3-5 accounts get the pre-GA
  build? Sales to propose.
- **Andes-only or RISC-V-broad**: hold v1.0 to Andes ISA only, or
  open the QEMU plugin layer to non-Andes RISC-V from day one?
- **Internal use revenue accounting**: how does internal Andes
  engineering use of the product show up in BU P&L?

---

## 13. References

- `FRS.md` - functional requirements (engineering contract)
- `commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - engineering plan
- `docs/limitation.md` - alpha envelope
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` - user-facing workflows
- ARM Cycle Models product page (competitive benchmark)
- Imperas / Synopsys RISC-V Reference Platform (competitive benchmark)
- gem5 KVM->O3CPU switch (reference architecture pattern)
- `~/work/Alioth/doc/alioth-vs-gem5.md` - mid-sim CPU swap gap

fast-forwards in QEMU, switches to cycle engine at ROI, returns a
cycle figure correlated with RTL within an explicit error budget.

- Acceptance: closed-source customer ELF round-trips; cycle figure
  agrees with fully-RTL baseline within 1% on the ROI window.

### MR-B - Linux + userspace ROI

Boot Linux, reach userspace hot loop, hand off to cycle engine,
measure, hand back to QEMU.

- Acceptance: at least 3 SPEC-class workloads under Linux userspace
  ship a cycle figure end-to-end.

### MR-C - Whole-program estimate via SimPoint

Long workload, no explicit ROI. SimPoint clustering picks
representative regions, cycle engine measures each, weighted
combine produces a whole-program estimate.

- Acceptance: weighted estimate within 5-10% of fully-RTL on at
  least 3 SPEC-class workloads.

### MR-D - Closed-source RTL protection (encryption)

Cycle engine is RTL-derived (via Verilator) but the shipped binary
must not allow recovery of Andes RTL or microarch internals.

- Acceptance: third-party reverse-engineering audit confirms no
  RTL recoverable from shipped binary; license + IP officer sign-off.

### MR-E - Andes vendor CSR and ACE parity

All customer-visible Andes vendor CSRs and ACE coherence flows
round-trip across the handoff with bit-exact semantics.

- Acceptance: vendor-CSR conformance test suite passes 100%; ACE
  coherence regression passes on multi-hart workloads.

### MR-F - Pipeline trace export (kanata)

Customer can record kanata-format pipeline traces for the cycle
window with output byte-identical to a fully-RTL baseline.

- Acceptance: kanata diff against fully-RTL baseline is empty for
  the post-warmup window.

### MR-G - Iterative microarch tweak loop

Architect changes a cycle-engine parameter (cache size, ROB depth),
rebuilds engine only, re-runs measurement against the same QEMU
checkpoint without re-running boot.

- Acceptance: edit-rebuild-measure cycle under 5 minutes on a
  reference workload.

### MR-H - Multi-hart support

At least 4 harts in the cycle engine with coherent state transport
through ACE.

- Acceptance: a 4-hart parallel kernel round-trips and produces a
  cycle figure within 1% of fully-RTL baseline.

### MR-I - Determinism and reproducibility

Identical inputs (ELF + config + seed) produce bit-identical cycle
counts and pipeline traces across runs and hosts.

- Acceptance: a reproducibility test suite runs the same workload
  on 3 different hosts; all outputs bit-identical.

### MR-J - CI / batch integration

The product runs unattended in a CI environment. License daemon,
checkpointing, error reporting, and exit codes are CI-friendly.

- Acceptance: a reference CI pipeline (GitLab / Jenkins) runs 20
  workloads in parallel, collects results, no manual intervention.

### MR-K - First-class observability

Every handoff, trigger, and state transport event is logged with
structured key=value format. Errors are actionable, not "internal
error".

- Acceptance: a deliberate state-corruption injection produces a
  log message identifying the corrupted register and the handoff
  phase. No silent failures.

---

## 8. Go-to-Market & Delivery

### 8.1 Design-partner phase (months 0-6 post-engineering complete)

- 3-5 named Andes customers under NDA evaluate pre-GA build
- Free use under design-partner agreement; required to give
  feedback and bug reports

### 8.2 Controlled GA (months 6-12)

### 8.3 Broad GA (year 2+)

- Academic SKU launches
- Add-on packs (multi-hart, vendor IP variants) release

### 8.4 Onboarding goal

Customer goes from license activation to first valid cycle figure
on their own workload in **under 1 working day** with documentation
alone, no FAE intervention.

# Hybrid Simulator - Functional Requirements Specification

Status: draft v0.1. Written 2026-05-29. Owner: Nick.
Audience: Engineering, QA, IP/Legal, Sales engineering.

Companion to `MRD.md` (commercial product view). This document is
the **engineering contract**: every shippable behavior of Andes
HybridSim v1.0, with one-line acceptance criteria per requirement.

Requirement IDs are stable across drafts. Each FR traces back to
one or more MR-x in MRD.md.

---

## 1. Scope and Definitions

### 1.1 In scope

Andes HybridSim v1.0, the commercial Tier-2 hybrid simulator
described in `MRD.md` sections 1-2. Specifically:

- `hsim` driver CLI
- QEMU (Andes fork) with hybrid plugin
- vsim cycle engine (Verilator-derived, encrypted)
- State transport library (`hybrid_state_v1`)
- Trigger toolkit (magic-CSR, PC-watch, icount, SimPoint)
- Pipeline trace converter (kanata, Clarity DB)
- License daemon
- Installer, documentation, sample workloads

### 1.2 Out of scope (v1.0)

- Non-Andes RISC-V ISA variants
- QEMU + Alioth (cycle-side Alioth) - documented as future in MRD
- FPGA backend
- Cloud-hosted SaaS delivery
- Multi-cluster cache coherence beyond a single Andes cluster
- Vector extension `V` beyond what AndeStar V5 covers

### 1.3 Definitions

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| ROI | Region of Interest. Window of dynamic instructions to measure cycle-exactly. |
| Fast engine | QEMU 9.x with Andes plugin. Runs non-ROI code. |
| Cycle engine | vsim, encrypted Verilator-derived binary. Runs ROI. |
| Handoff | Atomic state transfer between fast and cycle engine. |
| Trigger | A mechanism that fires the handoff (magic-CSR write, PC match, icount expiry, SimPoint marker). |
| Hybrid state | `hybrid_state_v1` wire format - GPR, FPR, V-state, CSR, PC, mem snapshot, timing baseline. |
| Cycle figure | The cycle count delta across the ROI window, returned to the user. |
| Warmup | Initial cycles after handoff where cache/predictor state is not yet steady; excluded from acceptance comparison. |

### 1.4 Traceability

Every FR includes a `Traces: MR-x [, MR-y...]` line tying it back
to `MRD.md`.

---

## 2. System Architecture Overview

```
+--------+   trigger   +----------+   handoff   +--------+
|  ELF   | ----------> |   QEMU   | ----------> |  vsim  |
| (cust) |             |  + plug  |  state +    | cycle  |
+--------+             +----------+   mem mmap  | engine |
                            ^                   +--------+
                            |   handback             |
                            +------------------------+
                                state + cycle count
```

Three phases per workload:
1. **QEMU1**: boot + setup, fast.
2. **vsim**: ROI, cycle-exact, encrypted.
3. **QEMU2**: post-ROI, fast (optional, for whole-program runs).

Shared substrate: `/dev/shm` mmap-backed RAM, file-descriptor
based state transport (`hybrid_state_v1`), license daemon over
network socket.

---

## 3. FR-1xx Functional Capabilities

### FR-101 - Three-phase handoff orchestration

`hsim run` shall execute the QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2 sequence
without user intervention beyond the initial invocation.

- Inputs: ELF, ROI specification (trigger config), workload args
- Output: cycle figure (decimal), exit code, optional pipeline trace
- Acceptance: a bare-metal kernel with PC-trigger round-trips end-to-end with exit code 0.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-G

### FR-102 - Trigger: magic-CSR write

A write to a configured CSR (default `0x7C0`, customer-configurable)
shall fire the QEMU->vsim handoff at the next instruction boundary.

- Acceptance: ELF that writes magic-CSR triggers handoff within 1 instruction; no false positives in 1B-cycle stress test.
- Traces: MR-A

### FR-103 - Trigger: PC watchpoint

A configured PC address shall fire the handoff at the matching
instruction without requiring source modification.

- Acceptance: closed-source ELF (no magic-CSR access) triggers correctly on PC match.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-D (closed-source customer ELFs)

### FR-104 - Trigger: instruction count

A configured icount threshold shall fire the handoff after N
dynamic instructions from a reference point.

- Acceptance: handoff fires at exactly icount=N, deterministic across runs.
- Traces: MR-C, MR-I

### FR-105 - Trigger: SimPoint cluster marker

The SimPoint clustering tool shall generate a per-cluster trigger
spec consumable by `hsim run --mode simpoint`.

- Acceptance: SimPoint output drives N handoffs at N cluster boundaries; per-cluster cycle figures collected and weight-combined.
- Traces: MR-C

### FR-106 - QEMU1 -> vsim handoff: full state transport

The following state shall transport bit-exactly from QEMU to vsim:

- 32 GPRs (RV64I)
- 32 FPRs (with NaN-boxing per RISC-V spec)
- V-state (vector regs + vcsr per AndeStar V5)
- All architectural CSRs reachable in supported privilege modes
- All Andes-vendor CSRs in the customer-visible list (see FR-401)
- PC
- Memory snapshot (shared mmap RAM)
- PMP config (read-only, enforced at vsim entry)
- Trap delegation state

- Acceptance: post-handoff vsim execution of `nop` produces identical architectural-visible state as a fully-RTL run from the same checkpoint.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-E, MR-I

### FR-107 - vsim -> QEMU2 handback

Symmetric to FR-106. State at vsim ROI exit shall be re-injected
into QEMU2 bit-exactly.

- Acceptance: bare-metal workload completes execution under QEMU2 after a vsim ROI window; final result matches fully-RTL baseline.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-G

### FR-108 - M-mode workload support

The v1.0 envelope shall include any RV64GC + AndeStar V5 workload
running entirely in M-mode with PMP-static, trap-free ROI.

- Acceptance: 10 representative M-mode kernels round-trip without error.
- Traces: MR-A

### FR-109 - S-mode and U-mode workload support

The v1.0 envelope shall extend to S-mode and U-mode workloads,
including supervisor page tables (Sv39/Sv48) and trap handling
inside the ROI.

- Acceptance: 3 Linux userspace workloads (SPEC-class) round-trip.
- Traces: MR-B

### FR-110 - Cycle figure reporting

After every successful run, `hsim` shall emit:
- Total ROI cycles (decimal)
- Per-phase wall-clock time
- SimPoint weighted estimate (when applicable)
- Confidence band on the estimate (95% CI)

- Acceptance: machine-parseable JSON report at `hsim.report.json`.
- Traces: MR-C, MR-J

### FR-111 - Pipeline trace export: kanata

When `--trace kanata` is set, the cycle engine shall emit kanata
format for the ROI window, byte-identical to a fully-RTL baseline
after warmup.

- Acceptance: `diff` against fully-RTL kanata is empty for the post-warmup window.
- Traces: MR-F

### FR-112 - Pipeline trace export: Clarity DB

When `--trace clarity` is set, the cycle engine shall emit a
Clarity-format pipeline DB for the ROI window.

- Acceptance: Clarity DB import into the Andes Clarity viewer succeeds; per-stage event counts match fully-RTL.
- Traces: MR-F

### FR-113 - Multi-hart ROI

`hsim` shall support ROIs that span >= 4 harts with coherent state
transport through ACE.

- Acceptance: a 4-hart kernel round-trips; cycle figure within 1% of fully-RTL baseline.
- Traces: MR-H

### FR-114 - Resumable / checkpointed runs

A long QEMU1 phase shall be checkpointable mid-run, so a customer
can boot once and re-enter vsim multiple times without re-booting.

- Acceptance: customer boots Linux once (~30 min), then runs 10
  different ROIs measured against the same checkpoint, with total
  wall-clock under 1 hour.
- Traces: MR-G

---

## 4. FR-2xx Performance Requirements

### FR-201 - Wall-clock speedup envelope

On a workload where the ROI is <= 1% of dynamic instructions,
HybridSim shall complete in <= 1% of the wall-clock time of a
vsim-alone run of the same workload.

- Acceptance: 3 reference workloads measured; speedup >= 100x.
- Traces: MR-A, MRD section 9.1

### FR-202 - Per-ROI accuracy

The cycle figure for the ROI window shall agree with a fully-RTL
baseline within 1% after a documented warmup tolerance.

- Acceptance: 5 reference ROIs; max error <= 1.0%.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-E

### FR-203 - SimPoint whole-program accuracy

The weighted whole-program estimate from SimPoint mode shall be
within 5-10% of fully-RTL on SPEC-class workloads.

- Acceptance: 3 SPEC-class workloads; max error <= 10%, average <= 5%.
- Traces: MR-C

### FR-204 - Time-to-first-result

A new customer with the installer and a sample workload shall
produce a valid cycle figure within 1 working day, with
documentation alone (no FAE involvement).

- Acceptance: timed user study with 3 fresh engineers; 100% reach valid figure within 8 hours.
- Traces: MRD section 8.4

### FR-205 - Iterative re-measurement latency

After an initial QEMU1 phase, a re-measurement of the same ROI
with an updated cycle engine shall complete in <= 5 minutes.

- Acceptance: edit-rebuild-measure cycle measured on 3 microarch parameter tweaks.
- Traces: MR-G

---

## 5. FR-3xx Interface Requirements

### FR-301 - `hsim` CLI

Top-level entry. Subcommands:
- `hsim run` - one-shot workload execution
- `hsim simpoint` - clustering + per-cluster runs + combine
- `hsim trace` - trace-only mode (kanata, clarity)
- `hsim checkpoint` - QEMU1 checkpoint management
- `hsim license` - license daemon control / diagnostics
- `hsim diag` - capture bug report bundle
- `hsim version` - prints versions of all components

- Acceptance: `--help` for every subcommand; exit codes per Unix convention.
- Traces: MR-J, MR-K

### FR-302 - Configuration file format

`hsim.config.yaml` shall specify trigger config, workload paths,
cycle-engine params, license server, output format. Schema-validated.

- Acceptance: bad config produces actionable error pointing at the offending line.
- Traces: MR-J, MR-K

### FR-303 - JSON output report

Every run shall emit `hsim.report.json` with the schema defined in
`docs/report-schema.json` (to be written).

- Acceptance: schema validation passes on every successful run.
- Traces: MR-J

### FR-304 - Programmatic API (Python binding)

A Python module shall expose the `hsim run` interface as a function
returning the report dict. For CI scripting.

- Acceptance: `import hsim; r = hsim.run(...)` returns a parsed report.
- Traces: MR-J

### FR-305 - Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | run succeeded, valid cycle figure |
| 1 | configuration error |
| 2 | license error |
| 3 | trigger never fired |
| 4 | state-transport corruption detected |
| 5 | cycle engine crashed |
| 6 | QEMU engine crashed |
| 7 | ROI exited unexpectedly |
| 9x | reserved |

- Acceptance: each documented failure produces the matching exit code in a fault-injection test.
- Traces: MR-J, MR-K

---

## 6. FR-4xx Compatibility Requirements

### FR-401 - Andes IP coverage

v1.0 shall support these Andes cores: AX25, AX27, AX45, AX46.
D23v deferred to v1.1.

For each core, the Andes vendor CSR set published in the AndeStar
V5 specification (revision frozen at v1.0 ship) shall round-trip
bit-exactly.

- Acceptance: vendor-CSR conformance test suite (~50 CSRs per core) passes 100%.
- Traces: MR-E

### FR-402 - ACE coherence support

Multi-hart workloads shall transport ACE coherence state
(directory + snoop filter) bit-exactly across the handoff.

- Acceptance: a coherent multi-hart test (e.g. shared-counter benchmark) produces identical results to fully-RTL.
- Traces: MR-E, MR-H

### FR-403 - Host OS support

v1.0 ships for x86_64 Linux only. Supported distros: Ubuntu 22.04
LTS, RHEL 8 and 9, SUSE SLES 15. No Windows, no macOS.

- Acceptance: install + smoke test passes on each supported distro.
- Traces: MRD section 8

### FR-404 - Toolchain compatibility

ELFs produced by:
- Andes GNU toolchain (current and previous release)
- Andes LLVM toolchain (current release)
- Upstream RISC-V GCC (current release)

shall be accepted.

- Acceptance: a benchmark built with each toolchain round-trips.
- Traces: MR-A

### FR-405 - QEMU upstream tracking

The QEMU engine shall be based on QEMU 9.x, with documented
patch set against upstream. Customer can rebuild from source under
NDA (source escrow).

- Acceptance: source tarball + patch series builds against upstream 9.x.
- Traces: MRD section 12 (QEMU dependency)

---

## 7. FR-5xx IP Protection Requirements

### FR-501 - Cycle-engine binary encryption

The vsim binary shall not allow recovery of Andes RTL or microarch
internals by static or dynamic analysis.

- Acceptance: third-party reverse-engineering audit; legal sign-off.
- Traces: MR-D

### FR-502 - Anti-debug / anti-instrumentation

The cycle engine shall refuse to execute under `ptrace`, `gdb`,
`strace`, dynamic tracing, or memory-introspection tools beyond
those explicitly whitelisted for support telemetry.

- Acceptance: attempted attach produces an actionable refusal log; no crash, no leak.
- Traces: MR-D

### FR-503 - State-transport encryption

`hybrid_state_v1` payload in `/dev/shm` shall be encrypted at rest
with a session key derived from license activation. Plaintext
visible only within the cycle engine address space.

- Acceptance: external readers of `/dev/shm` see ciphertext; the cycle engine reads it correctly.
- Traces: MR-D

### FR-504 - License key binding

The cycle engine binary shall refuse to execute without a valid
license check-out from the license daemon. License key is bound to
host MAC + HSM (node-locked) or floating pool (network).

- Acceptance: missing or invalid license produces exit code 2 with a clear message.
- Traces: MR-J, MRD section 6.2

### FR-505 - License feature flags

License records shall carry per-feature flags:
- core support pack (which Andes cores)
- kanata export
- SimPoint
- multi-hart
- premium SLA (telemetry-routed)

Cycle engine shall enforce flags at runtime.

- Acceptance: a license without kanata flag refuses `--trace kanata` with exit 2.
- Traces: MRD section 6.2

### FR-506 - License expiry

License expiry shall:
1. Refuse new runs (exit code 2).
2. Allow in-progress runs to complete with a warning log.
3. Not corrupt or drop reports already written to disk.

- Acceptance: clock-skew test (advance host clock past expiry mid-run) shows graceful behavior per spec.
- Traces: MRD section 6.2

### FR-507 - Source escrow

For top-tier customers, source for the cycle engine shall be
deposited with a neutral escrow agent and released on documented
trigger events (e.g. Andes EOL of the product).

- Acceptance: escrow agreement signed; release procedure documented.
- Traces: MRD section 12

---

## 8. FR-6xx Quality & Observability

### FR-601 - Structured logging

Every internal event (trigger fire, handoff begin/end, state
transport, license check, error) shall log in the format
`[Tag] evt=<ns>.<action> key=value ...`.

- Acceptance: a regex-based log validator passes on a sample run.
- Traces: MR-K

### FR-602 - Log levels

Log levels: ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, TRACE. Default INFO. Settable
via `--log-level` or `HSIM_LOG_LEVEL` env.

- Acceptance: level filtering observable on a sample run.
- Traces: MR-K

### FR-603 - Bug report bundle

`hsim diag` shall capture:
- All log files
- The active config
- The `hybrid_state_v1` snapshot (encrypted, support-only readable)
- Host info (uname, distro, libc, kernel, license daemon state)
- Reproducer ELF and config (with customer opt-in)

into a single tarball ready to attach to a support ticket.

- Acceptance: support reproduces a customer-reported bug from a `hsim diag` bundle alone.
- Traces: MR-K

### FR-604 - Deterministic mode

When `--deterministic` is set, every run with the same inputs
produces bit-identical cycle figure, pipeline trace, and report
across hosts and runs.

- Acceptance: cross-host reproducibility test (3 hosts) passes.
- Traces: MR-I

### FR-605 - Error message quality bar

Every fatal error shall include:
- a unique error code (e.g. `HSIM-E0042`)
- a one-line description
- a pointer to the doc section that explains it
- the suspected failing component
- recommended next step (retry, contact support, check config)

- Acceptance: a sample of 20 deliberate errors are graded against the bar; >= 90% pass.
- Traces: MR-K

### FR-606 - Telemetry (opt-in)

With explicit customer opt-in, `hsim` may transmit anonymized
usage data (workload size, success/failure code, host info) to
Andes telemetry endpoint. Default off.

- Acceptance: telemetry disabled by default; opt-in via config flag; payload schema documented and signed-off by legal.
- Traces: MRD section 8

---

## 9. FR-7xx Packaging & Delivery

### FR-701 - Installer

A single self-extracting installer (`.run` or `.deb` / `.rpm`)
shall install all components into a configurable prefix, register
the license daemon, and run a post-install smoke test.

- Acceptance: fresh-host install on each supported distro completes in <= 5 minutes and passes the smoke test.
- Traces: MRD section 8

### FR-702 - Dependency footprint

The installer shall declare all external runtime dependencies.
Anything not in the base distro must be bundled.

- Acceptance: dependency audit passes; no surprise yum/apt requirements at runtime.
- Traces: MRD section 8

### FR-703 - Upgrade in place

A version N+1 installer over version N shall preserve config,
license, and existing checkpoints; report any incompatibilities
explicitly.

- Acceptance: N -> N+1 upgrade test on each supported distro; checkpoints from N work on N+1 or produce a documented error.
- Traces: MR-G, MRD section 8

### FR-704 - Uninstaller

Clean uninstall shall remove all installed files, license records,
and daemons. User-generated data (reports, checkpoints) preserved
unless explicitly removed.

- Acceptance: post-uninstall, no `hsim` binaries on path; no daemons running.
- Traces: MRD section 8

### FR-705 - Documentation set

Shipped with installer:
- Installation guide
- User guide (mirrors `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`)
- ABI reference (`hybrid_state_v1`, trigger spec, report schema)
- Integration guide (CI, Python API)
- Limitations document (current envelope from `limitation.md`)
- Error code reference (from FR-605)
- Release notes per version

- Acceptance: documentation review by an external technical writer signs off readability.
- Traces: MRD section 8.4

---

## 10. FR-8xx Support & Lifecycle

### FR-801 - Versioning

Semantic versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. ABI breaks bump MAJOR.

- Acceptance: version policy documented; any ABI break is gated by a code review checklist.
- Traces: MRD section 8

### FR-802 - Support tiers

| Tier | Response | Channels |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | 3 business days | email, web ticket |
| Premium | 1 business day | email, web ticket, named FAE |
| Mission Critical | 4 hours | phone, dedicated FAE, war-room access |

- Acceptance: each tier has a documented SLA and escalation path.
- Traces: MRD section 6.1

### FR-803 - EOL policy

Each MAJOR version shall be supported for >= 3 years from GA; EOL
announced >= 12 months in advance.

- Acceptance: EOL policy published; reflected in license terms.
- Traces: MRD section 8

### FR-804 - Patch release cadence

PATCH releases every 4 weeks for v1.0; MINOR releases every quarter.

- Acceptance: release cadence documented and trackable in CI.
- Traces: MRD section 8.2

---

## 11. FR-9xx Security & Compliance

### FR-901 - License server security

The license daemon shall:
- TLS 1.3 for all network communication
- HSM-bound private keys
- Logged audit trail of every check-out / check-in

- Acceptance: third-party security audit; OWASP Top 10 review.
- Traces: MRD section 6.2

### FR-902 - Open-source compliance

For every OSS component shipped, the installer shall include:
- License text
- Source pointer (URL or escrow)
- Modification disclosure (for LGPL components like Verilator)

- Acceptance: OSS compliance audit by Andes legal.
- Traces: MRD section 10 (Verilator licensing review)

### FR-903 - Export control

Product classification reviewed for US EAR / ITAR; documented ECCN.
Installer enforces destination country checks where required.

- Acceptance: export control review by Andes legal; ECCN documented in product sheet.
- Traces: MRD section 6.3

### FR-904 - Supply chain integrity

All shipped binaries shall be signed with an Andes code-signing
certificate. Installer verifies signatures before extraction.

- Acceptance: signature verification on every install; tampered installer is refused with a clear message.
- Traces: MR-D, MR-K

---

## 12. Acceptance Test Matrix

Mapping FR to test suites. Each test suite is owned by a named
engineer; pass/fail tracked in CI dashboard before any release.

| Suite | Covers | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| smoke | FR-101, FR-204, FR-701, FR-702 | tbd |
| state-transport | FR-106, FR-107, FR-401, FR-402 | tbd |
| trigger | FR-102, FR-103, FR-104, FR-105 | tbd |
| accuracy | FR-202, FR-203 | tbd |
| simpoint | FR-105, FR-203 | tbd |
| multi-hart | FR-113, FR-402 | tbd |
| trace | FR-111, FR-112 | tbd |
| determinism | FR-604, FR-203 | tbd |
| license | FR-504, FR-505, FR-506 | tbd |
| ip-protection | FR-501, FR-502, FR-503 | tbd |
| installer | FR-701, FR-702, FR-703, FR-704 | tbd |
| docs | FR-705 | tbd |
| security | FR-901, FR-902, FR-903, FR-904 | tbd |

---

## 13. Traceability Matrix (MR -> FR)

| MR | Description | FRs |
|---|---|---|
| MR-A | Cycle-exact ROI on customer workloads | FR-101, FR-102, FR-103, FR-106, FR-108, FR-202, FR-404 |
| MR-B | Linux + userspace ROI | FR-109 |
| MR-C | Whole-program estimate via SimPoint | FR-104, FR-105, FR-110, FR-203 |
| MR-D | RTL protection / encryption | FR-501, FR-502, FR-503, FR-904 |
| MR-E | Andes vendor CSR + ACE parity | FR-401, FR-402, FR-106 |
| MR-F | Pipeline trace export | FR-111, FR-112 |
| MR-G | Iterative microarch tweak | FR-101, FR-114, FR-205, FR-703 |
| MR-H | Multi-hart | FR-113, FR-402 |
| MR-I | Determinism | FR-104, FR-106, FR-604 |
| MR-J | CI / batch integration | FR-301, FR-302, FR-303, FR-304, FR-305, FR-504, FR-606 |
| MR-K | First-class observability | FR-601, FR-602, FR-603, FR-605, FR-904 |

Every MR has at least 2 supporting FRs. Every FR traces back to
at least one MR. No orphan requirements.

---

## 14. Open Engineering Questions

For Engineering / IP officer review:

- **Encryption mechanism**: in-house obfuscation pass on Verilator
  output, or external Carbon-style partner? Trade-off:
  build-vs-buy, royalty vs salary, time-to-market.
- **License daemon**: build on FlexLM (industry standard but
  licensing fee), Reprise RLM, or in-house? FlexLM has highest
  customer acceptance.
- **State-transport encryption key**: derive from license daemon
  on each run, or fixed per install? Per-run is more secure but
  adds latency.
- **vsim binary size**: encrypted output is typically 2-5x source
  size; what is the acceptable footprint?
- **Multi-hart determinism**: scheduling order in vsim cycle engine
  is deterministic given seed; QEMU side may not be. Strategy?
- **Vendor CSR list**: FR-401 says "published in AndeStar V5"; need
  a frozen list per core for the v1.0 commit.
- **Source escrow**: which neutral agent (Iron Mountain, NCC, etc)
  and what are the customer-facing trigger conditions?

- `MRD.md` - commercial market requirements
- `commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - engineering plan
- `docs/limitation.md` - current envelope
- `hybrid_plan.md` - architecture and rationale
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` - user-facing workflow doc
- AndeStar V5 specification (vendor CSR list source of truth)
- Verilator commercial use guidelines (LGPL review)
- FlexLM and Reprise RLM documentation (license daemon options)
